<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="" />{{rh|48|THE GOSPEL|CHA. XVII.}}</noinclude>{{c|{{larger|{{sc|Chap. XVII.}}}}}}

{{c|''As he promised, he giueth them a sight of the glorie, vnto which Suffering doth bring: 9 and then againe doth inculcate his Passion. 14 A deuil also he casteth out which his Disciples could not for their incredulitie and lacke of praying and fasting. 22 being yet in Galilee, he reuealeth more about his Passion. 24 and the tribute that the Collectors exacted for al, he payeth for him self and Peter: declaring yet withal his freedom both by word and miracle.''}} {{verse|chapter=17|verse=1}}{{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=The TRANSFIGVRATION of our Lord, celebrated in the Church the 6. of Aug. The Gospel of the said feast, & of the 2. Sunday in Lent: and on the Saterday before.}}AND after six dayes {{sc|Iesvs}} taketh vnto him Peter and Iames and Iohn his brother, and bringeth them into a high mountaine apart:{{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''Mr. 9, 2. Luc. 9, 28.''}} {{verse|chapter=17|verse=2}}† And he vvas {{sup|‖}} transfigured before them. And his face did shine as the sunne: & his garments became vvhite as snow.{{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''2. Pet. 1, 17.''}} {{verse|chapter=17|verse=3}}† And behold there {{sup|‖}} appeared to them Moyses and Elias talking vvith him. {{verse|chapter=17|verse=4}}† And Peter ansvvering, said to {{sc|Iesvs}}, Lord, it is good for vs to be here: if thou vvilt, let vs make here three tabernacles, one for thee, and one for Moyses, and one for Elias. {{verse|chapter=17|verse=5}}† And as he vvas yet speaking, behold a bright cloude ouershadovved them. And loe a voice out of the cloude, saying. This is my vvelbeloued sonne, in vvhom I am vvel pleased: heare ye him. {{verse|chapter=17|verse=6}}† And the disciples hearing it, fel vpon their face, and vvere sore afraid. {{verse|chapter=17|verse=7}}† And {{sc|Iesvs}} came and touched them: and he said to them, Arise, and feare not. {{verse|chapter=17|verse=8}}† And they lifting vp their eyes, savv no body, but only {{sc|Iesvs}}. {{verse|chapter=17|verse=9}}† And as they descended from the {{sup|‖}} mount, {{sc|Iesvs}} commaunded them, saying, Tel the vision to no body, til the Sonne of man be risen from the dead.⊣

{{verse|chapter=17|verse=10}}† And his Disciples asked him, saying, What say the Scribes then, that {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''Mal. 4, 5.''}}* Elias must come first? {{verse|chapter=17|verse=11}}† But he ansvvering, said to them, {{sup|‖}} Elias in deede shal come, and restore al things. {{verse|chapter=17|verse=12}}† And I say to you, that Elias is already come, and they did not knovv him, but vvrought on him vvhatsoeuer they vvould. So also the Sonne of man shal suffer of them. {{verse|chapter=17|verse=13}}† Then the Disciples vnderstoode, that of Iohn the Baptist he had spoken to them.

{{verse|chapter=17|verse=14}}† And {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=''Mar. 9, 14. Luc. 9, 37.''}}* vvhen he vvas come vnto the multitude, there came to him a man falling dovvne vpon his knees before him, {{verse|chapter=17|verse=15}}† saying, Lord haue mercie vpon my sonne, for he is lunatike, and sore vexed: for he falleth often into the fire, and often into the vvater. {{verse|chapter=17|verse=16}}† and I offered him to thy Disciples: and they could not cure him. {{verse|chapter=17|verse=17}}† {{sc|Iesvs}} ansvvered and said, O faithles and peruerse generation, hovv long shal I be vvith<noinclude>{{rh|||you?}}</noinclude>
